name: Taj Mahal
kicker: White marble mausoleum in Agra · Built by Shah Jahan for his wife
briefing: Shah Jahan, the Mughal emperor of India, built the Taj Mahal as a tomb for his wife Mumtaz Mahal, who died giving birth to their fourteenth child. Finished around 1653 after nearly twenty years of work by thousands of artisans, its white marble walls are inlaid with colorful gemstones in floral patterns. Today the Taj Mahal stands in Agra as one of the New Seven Wonders of the World and a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

sample.note: 3 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (1 Middle School/Easy High School + 2 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: One inscription inside this structure states that its occupant “journeyed to the banquet hall of eternity” in the Islamic year 1076. Its builder was deposed by his son Aurangzeb and imprisoned at nearby Agra Fort, from which legend says he could still glimpse this monument.
tossups.r: He was eventually buried inside it beside his wife. For 10 points, name this white marble mausoleum in Agra, India, built by Shah Jahan for Mumtaz Mahal.

tossups.p: The chief architect of this structure is traditionally identified as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri, though Makramat Khan also helped supervise its construction. A calligrapher named Amanat Khan decorated its surfaces with lines from the Quran.
tossups.r: Construction of this mausoleum took about twenty years and employed roughly twenty thousand workers. For 10 points, name this white marble monument that Mughal emperor Shah Jahan built on the Yamuna River in Agra, India.

tossups.p: Legend holds that this monument’s builder planned a black twin version of it on the opposite bank of the river, a structure that was never built. A garden called the Mehtab Bagh sits aligned with it across that same river.
tossups.r: Its four minarets lean slightly outward from its central dome, and a long reflecting pool lined with cypress trees leads up to its entrance. For 10 points, name this white mausoleum built on the Yamuna River by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

tossups.p: This structure’s main gateway, built of red sandstone, bears a Quranic inscription said to invite the faithful into paradise. Its white marble walls are inlaid with colorful gemstones arranged in floral patterns.
tossups.r: The complex also includes a mosque and a matching guest house flanking the central tomb. For 10 points, name this mausoleum in Agra, India, that Shah Jahan built for his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

tossups.p: The woman honored by this structure died in 1631 shortly after giving birth to her fourteenth child, and her husband was eventually entombed here beside her. A pollution-control zone known as the Trapezium Zone now limits nearby industry to help protect its marble from discoloring.
tossups.r: This monument’s name is often translated as “Crown of the Palace.” For 10 points, identify this white mausoleum on the Yamuna River in Agra, India, built by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan.

tossups.p: A gilded finial atop this structure’s central dome combines an Islamic crescent shape with a lotus design inspired by Hindu temple art. The wife this place honors was born Arjumand Banu Begum before her marriage to a future Mughal emperor.
tossups.r: This site is closed to visitors every Friday, when its on-site mosque holds prayers. For 10 points, name this gleaming white mausoleum that Shah Jahan built in Agra, India.

tossups.p: Poet Rabindranath Tagore [“tuh-GORE”] called this structure “a teardrop on the cheek of time.” It blends Persian, Islamic, and Indian architectural styles around a central white dome.
tossups.r: The structure appears pink at sunrise, bright white at midday, and golden under moonlight. For 10 points, name this mausoleum built on the Yamuna River in Agra, India, by Shah Jahan for his wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

tossups.p: This structure’s complex includes a red sandstone gateway, a mosque, and a matching guest house arranged around formal Mughal gardens. Its four slightly outward-leaning minarets flank a central onion-shaped dome.
tossups.r: A long reflecting pool lined with cypress trees runs toward its entrance. For 10 points, name this white marble mausoleum in Agra, India, built for Shah Jahan’s wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

tossups.p: Calligrapher Amanat Khan signed his name into the Quranic inscriptions covering parts of this structure, one of the few artisans here known to have done so. Its chief architect is usually identified as Ustad Ahmad Lahauri.
tossups.r: The whole complex took shape over roughly twenty years on the banks of the Yamuna River. For 10 points, name this Agra landmark built by Shah Jahan as a tomb for Mumtaz Mahal.

tossups.r: Four minarets stand guard at its corners above a long, cypress-lined reflecting pool. For 10 points, name this white marble mausoleum built on the Yamuna River in Agra, India, by Shah Jahan for his late wife, Mumtaz Mahal.

trap.title: The building or the woman?
trap.body: Taj Mahal is only the mausoleum itself. Mumtaz Mahal, the wife it was built for, and Shah Jahan, the emperor who built it, are different people with different answer lines. A clue about construction, architecture, or materials wants the building; a clue about a person’s life or death wants the person.
trap.fix: Listen for the noun. “This structure,” “this monument,” or “this mausoleum” means the building. “This empress” or “this emperor” means the person. Marble, minarets, and Agra point to the building.
